entries.title: Inspect the data before changing the model

sources.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page
sources.locator: The recipe, section 1: Become one with the data

entries.takeaway: Karpathy recommends examining real examples, distributions and outliers before building a model; duplicate or corrupted inputs can explain failures.
entries.editorial_application: For an AI coding project, inspect representative inputs and failure cases before changing prompts or architecture. This is an editorial application.
entries.caveat: The source concerns neural-network training. Do not generalize its dated architecture or optimizer advice into current best practice.

entries.title: Prove the smallest pipeline works

sources.title: A Recipe for Training Neural Networks
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page
sources.locator: The recipe, section 2: overfit one batch and visualize just before the net

entries.takeaway: Karpathy suggests overfitting a tiny batch and inspecting the exact model inputs to expose pipeline bugs before scaling.
entries.editorial_application: Create a small, known-answer test case before expanding an AI workflow. A passing demo still needs separate generalization checks.
entries.caveat: A tiny training-set fit is a debugging check, not evidence of production quality. Keep this distinct from inspecting dataset quality.

entries.title: Build capability through pilots and training

sources.title: Introducing the AI Transformation Playbook
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page

entries.takeaway: Ng sequences AI transformation through pilot projects, an internal AI team, broad training, strategy, and communication, with sustained investment.
entries.editorial_application: Choose a bounded pilot, then identify the team skills and communication needed to turn it into repeatable capability. This is an editorial application.
entries.caveat: This is an evergreen 2018 roadmap, not a new announcement or a universal fixed implementation timetable.

entries.title: Learn from the structure already in data

sources.title: Self-supervised learning: The dark matter of intelligence
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page
sources.locator: Self-supervised learning is predictive learning; author byline

entries.takeaway: LeCun and Misra describe self-supervision as learning to predict hidden aspects from observed data, reducing dependence on manually supplied labels.
entries.editorial_application: When planning an AI project, distinguish the broad representations learned in pretraining from evidence needed to validate the actual task.
entries.caveat: Coauthored research perspective from 2021. The authors present a promising research direction, not proof of human-level intelligence or label-free deployment.

entries.title: Build on distinctive domain knowledge

sources.title: Arm Yourself With Specific Knowledge
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page
sources.locator: Naval replies under specific knowledge and genuine curiosity

entries.takeaway: Naval connects distinctive expertise to curiosity, experience and judgment in a domain, rather than simply pursuing whichever skill is fashionable.
entries.editorial_application: Pair AI tooling with a domain you understand deeply; evaluate whether the tool improves a real problem there. This is an editorial application.
entries.caveat: Career philosophy, not a guaranteed earnings claim. The AI application is not a quotation or original claim from the 2019 discussion.

entries.title: Own the result, including failure

sources.title: Accountability Means Letting People Criticize You
sources.original_date_basis: Date displayed on original publisher page
sources.locator: Opening Q&A, first three Naval paragraphs

entries.takeaway: Naval frames accountability as accepting criticism and the possibility of failure; he says it can be practiced within an existing career.
entries.editorial_application: For a team experiment, state who owns the outcome and how mistakes will be reviewed. This is an editorial application.
entries.caveat: Personal business philosophy. Accountability should not be equated with blame, public humiliation or taking unapproved risks.

entries.title: Separate automatic checks from human judgment

sources.title: Formal Verification Meets Unverifiable Judgement
sources.original_date_basis: Original date recorded in the 18 October revised public report; original page fetch returned 403 in this seed pass
sources.locator: Referenced and summarized in 18 October revised report, thinker perspectives section

entries.takeaway: The archived briefing attributes to Ng a distinction between automatically checkable tasks and work requiring human judgment.
entries.editorial_application: The 18 October report applied the distinction to deciding which parts of an AI trial can be checked automatically.
entries.caveat: Already covered publicly. Podcast narration is unconfirmed; do not relabel the concept unused. Re-read the primary letter before any new detailed quotation.
